messages:
Alex: Heads-up — we need a quick cross-team call on the new metrics surface + sharing scopes for dashboards. Who should own the mapping between runtime signals and what shows up in customer vs internal views? cc @priya @jamie @sasha
Priya: I can own the product side for customer-facing spec. main Q: do we allow customers to see routing policy decisions (region, tier) or only outcome metrics? :thinking_face:
Jamie: From security/audit POV customers can see outcomes but not internal routing reasons. We do need to surface model_variant and model_hash for reproducibility, and all accesses logged. :lock:
Sasha: Runtime feels OK exposing p50/p95/p99, token cost, model_variant, and error breakdown by class. We should NOT expose node-level hostnames or queue depths in customer UI. Internal dashboard can show that.
Alex: Good, so split: customer view = outcome metrics + anonymized cost; internal view = everything including infra signals. Need to make this enforceable via RBAC and the sharing UI. Thoughts on policy shape?
Priya: Proposing simple scopes: `customer_read`, `internal_read`, `audit_view`. Customers get `customer_read`; internal ops + SRE get `internal_read`; security + compliance get `audit_view`.
Jamie: That maps well. Also must ensure audit_view always includes raw logs and change history for share links. We should tie audit tokens to an append-only export.
Sasha: Implementation note: runtime will emit the following labels per request: `region`, `model_variant`, `quant_profile`, `route_bucket`. We can map which labels are surfaced per scope. Example policy (pseudocode):
```
policies:
  customer_read:
    expose: [p50,p95,p99,token_cost,error_rate,model_variant]
  internal_read:
    expose: [*]
  audit_view:
    expose: [raw_logs,config_changes,share_history]
```
Priya: UX question — when a user shares a dashboard externally, should we automatically strip internal-only widgets or show a warning? I'd prefer strip + preview that shows what external viewers will see. :warning:
Alex: Strip + preview sounds good. Also add an explicit audit trail entry when a share link is created with who, what scope, and TTL.
Jamie: Agree. For compliance, TTL and exportability matter. Also require an approval workflow for any share that grants more than `customer_read` to external parties.
deploy-bot: NOTE: new audit log table `dashboard_shares` created. Columns: `share_id`, `creator`, `scope`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `preview_hash`.
Sasha: One more runtime detail — when we anonymize cost for customers, do we show a normalized cost per 1k tokens or an absolute dollar figure? We should prefer normalized units and optional absolute for enterprise-only.
Priya: Normalized default, absolute behind `billing:enterprise` flag. We'll add that to the product spec.
Alex: Action items: 1) Priya to draft product share UX with preview + default strip (due EOD +1). 2) Sasha to publish runtime label whitelist + anonymization rules (due +3). 3) Jamie to define audit schema + approval gate (due +3). 4) I'll schedule 30m sync. If anyone objects to the split scope/policy, say now. :eyes:
